issues.title: stringify() writes wrong block scalar indentation indicator for mapping values with indent other than 2
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

With an `indent` option other than 2, `stringify()` writes a block scalar mapping value whose first line starts with a space using the indentation indicator `2`. The content is written one indentation step right of the key, though, so the indicator and the content disagree. `parse()` then reads every line with extra leading spaces, or throws.

### To Reproduce

```js
import { parse, stringify } from 'yaml'

const value = { k: '  lead\nx\n' }

stringify(value, { indent: 4 })
// 'k: |2\n      lead\n    x\n'
parse(stringify(value, { indent: 4 }))
// { k: '    lead\n  x\n' }   ❌ two extra spaces on every line

parse(stringify(value, { indent: 3 }))
// { k: '   lead\n x\n' }     ❌ one extra space on every line

parse(stringify(value, { indent: 1 }))
// ❌ throws YAMLParseError: All mapping items must start at the same column
```

Nested mapping values and folded scalars (`blockQuote: 'folded'`) behave the same:

```js
parse(stringify({ a: { k: '  lead\nx\n' } }, { indent: 4 }))
// { a: { k: '    lead\n  x\n' } }   ❌

parse(stringify({ k: '  lead\nx' }, { indent: 4, blockQuote: 'folded' }))
// { k: '    lead\n  x' }   ❌
```

Sequence items round-trip at any indent (`stringify(['  lead\nx\n'], { indent: 4 })` → `'- |2\n    lead\n  x\n'`), as their content is two columns right of the `-`.

### Expected behaviour

`parse(stringify(value, { indent }))` equals `value`. For a mapping value, the indicator is the indentation step (e.g. `k: |4` for `indent: 4`), as the indentation indicator is relative to the parent node's indentation (YAML 1.2.2 §8.1.1.1), and the content is written one indentation step right of the key.

### Versions

- `yaml` 2.9.1 and 3.0.0-2
- Node.js 26.3.1

The indicator is computed in `blockString()` in `src/stringify/stringifyString.ts` as `const indentSize = indent ? '2' : '1'`, which is still on `main`. The top-level case (`'1'`) is #692.
